question: Should OpenClaw adopt this Kova revision as the default despite its known stale-live PID attribution gap, or wait for an ownership-safe upstream revision?
rationale: The patch is mechanically consistent, but only maintainers can decide whether potentially misleading resource evidence is acceptable before the upstream repair lands.

options.title: Fix Kova before pinning
options.body: Land bounded gateway-ownership revalidation and replacement-PID coverage upstream, rerun the release workflow, and pin the repaired immutable SHA.

options.title: Accept attribution uncertainty
options.body: Merge this revision while explicitly accepting that gateway transitions or PID reuse can make resource attribution inaccurate.

options.title: Keep only safe optimization
options.body: Create an upstream revision retaining report compaction but omitting the unsafe PID cache, then pin that revision.

recommendation.title: Fix Kova before pinning
recommendation.body: Land bounded gateway-ownership revalidation and replacement-PID coverage upstream, rerun the release workflow, and pin the repaired immutable SHA.

likelyOwner.reason: They own both the upstream optimization and this consuming pin, making them best positioned to repair and revalidate the dependency contract.
